world.title: Iran rejects uranium transfer as Pakistan seeks to restart US talks
world.summary: Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei told visiting Pakistani army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir on Tuesday that no enriched nuclear material would leave Iran. Iranian leaders said Tehran would not resume talks with Washington until the United States met its conditions. Iran’s demands include an end to hostilities acro
world.content: Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei told visiting Pakistani army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir on Tuesday that no enriched nuclear material would leave Iran. Iranian leaders said Tehran would not resume talks with Washington until the United States met its conditions. Iran’s demands include an end to hostilities across the region, the lifting of sanctions on its oil exports and the release of frozen Iranian assets. Munir’s visit is part of Pakistan’s effort to restart negotiations after a June memorandum of understanding collapsed when fighting resumed weeks later. Indirect talks at the United Nations General Assembly also failed to produce a breakthrough. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Washington must remove threats and sanctions before dialogue can begin. Separately, Qatar and Pakistan submitted a new proposal that sources told The New Arab had received positive responses from both governments. The reported plan would pair an unannounced International Atomic Energy Agency inspection with US permission for Iran to receive interest on $6 billion in frozen assets held in Qatar.

world.title: U.S. Secretary of State Rubio says U.S.-India trade deal is weeks away
world.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in Mumbai on Oct. 20 that Washington and New Delhi were close to a trade agreement, with a few details unresolved. President Donald Trump separately called a deal “pretty close” and said it could differ from previous pacts. Rubio said he expected the remaining work to take weeks
world.content: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in Mumbai on Oct. 20 that Washington and New Delhi were close to a trade agreement, with a few details unresolved. President Donald Trump separately called a deal “pretty close” and said it could differ from previous pacts. Rubio said he expected the remaining work to take weeks, not months, but the two sides signed no agreement during his visit. Rubio and Indian External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar also discussed energy security, defence, technology and regional issues. Rubio urged India to buy more U.S. energy and defence technology and proposed talks with Reliance Industries about processing more Venezuelan crude at its Jamnagar refinery. Tariffs and immigration restrictions have strained ties, and the two countries disagree over India’s continued purchases of Russian oil. India’s foreign ministry said both sides welcomed progress in negotiations and renewed their commitment to concluding them soon. A sticking point for New Delhi is securing tariff treatment that allows its exporters to compete with suppliers such as Vietnam and Bangladesh. The two governments have not announced a signing date.
world.image_alt: U.S. Secretary of State Rubio says U.S.-India trade deal is weeks away

world.title: Alberta premier rules out another separation vote after voters reject process
world.summary: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said she will not call another separation referendum while she remains in office, after voters rejected starting a legal process toward a possible break from Canada by roughly 75% to 25% in unofficial results. The nonbinding Oct. 19 ballot did not decide independence; it asked whether Alb
world.content: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said she will not call another separation referendum while she remains in office, after voters rejected starting a legal process toward a possible break from Canada by roughly 75% to 25% in unofficial results. The nonbinding Oct. 19 ballot did not decide independence; it asked whether Alberta should begin steps toward a later binding vote. More than 1.9 million ballots had been counted. Smith said Alberta would continue seeking greater provincial autonomy but resolve disputes with Ottawa through Canada’s political and legal institutions. She also said her government would pursue reforms approved on the ballot’s nine other questions, including immigration measures, while votes on constitutional proposals were still being counted. Prime Minister Mark Carney and Smith are also working on a proposed pipeline to move Alberta oil to the Pacific coast for export to Asian markets. Separatist leaders say they will continue organizing. Alberta Prosperity Project leader Jeffrey Rath has called for taking control of the governing United Conservative Party (UCP), while Let’s Talk Alberta founder Chris Scott said an immediate bid to take over the government and force another referendum would fail. Elections Alberta’s official results are scheduled for Oct. 29, and the UCP’s annual gathering in Calgary is due next month.
world.image_alt: Alberta premier rules out another separation vote after voters reject process

world.title: Australian MP Helen Haines loses both legs in alleged targeted car attack
world.summary: Independent Australian MP Helen Haines lost both legs after a driver allegedly struck her twice with a vehicle outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on Oct. 19. Her husband, Phil Haines, said Wednesday she was stable but remained in critical condition. Police allege the attack was targeted. Witnesses s
world.content: Independent Australian MP Helen Haines lost both legs after a driver allegedly struck her twice with a vehicle outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on Oct. 19. Her husband, Phil Haines, said Wednesday she was stable but remained in critical condition. Police allege the attack was targeted. Witnesses said the driver turned around and hit her again, and bystanders restrained him. Brendan Nugent, 43, appeared in Wangaratta Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday on charges including intentionally causing serious injury, dangerous driving causing serious injury and harming a public official. Court filings also list cannabis cultivation and possession charges. Nugent did not seek bail, and the court adjourned his case to Feb. 4, 2027. His lawyer told the court Nugent had a rare neurological condition, concussion and mental health concerns. Victoria Police say they found no prior direct contact between Nugent and Haines, and federal police say they had no specific intelligence indicating an imminent threat. The motive remains under investigation. Police describe the attack as apparently isolated and have not ruled out further serious charges.
world.image_alt: Australian MP Helen Haines loses both legs in alleged targeted car attack

world.title: SpaceX founder Musk reportedly capped Ukraine military satellite speeds, disrupting drones
world.summary: SpaceX founder Elon Musk ordered a speed cap on Starshield, SpaceX’s military-grade satellite service used by Ukraine, disrupting some Ukrainian attack and interceptor drone missions, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing U.S. officials and people familiar with the decision. Some U.S. officials said Musk acted on hi
world.content: SpaceX founder Elon Musk ordered a speed cap on Starshield, SpaceX’s military-grade satellite service used by Ukraine, disrupting some Ukrainian attack and interceptor drone missions, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing U.S. officials and people familiar with the decision. Some U.S. officials said Musk acted on his own, while another source said he spoke with senior administration officials, including President Donald Trump, before the change. The Journal also reported that Trump and Musk spoke after the slowdown became public. Ukraine uses the satellite connection for battlefield communications and drone operations. Ukrainian officials said the restrictions impaired missions, including efforts to intercept Russian attack drones; one Ukrainian analyst estimated that the degradation caused tens of millions of dollars in losses. Trump has warned Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy against strikes on Russian refineries. Trump has denied ordering the change, and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the Pentagon issued no directive, citing service terms instead. Zelenskyy said he raised restoring Starlink and Starshield service with Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Oslo on Oct. 20. Who authorized the restrictions remains disputed.
world.image_alt: SpaceX founder Musk reportedly capped Ukraine military satellite speeds, disrupting drones

world.title: UK sends Typhoon jets to shield Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
world.summary: The United Kingdom will deploy Royal Air Force Typhoon fighter jets to Saudi Arabia to intercept Houthi missiles and drones threatening cities and infrastructure, Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s government said Tuesday. The jets will fly defensive missions and will not strike Houthi targets in Yemen. Britain is also send
world.content: The United Kingdom will deploy Royal Air Force Typhoon fighter jets to Saudi Arabia to intercept Houthi missiles and drones threatening cities and infrastructure, Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s government said Tuesday. The jets will fly defensive missions and will not strike Houthi targets in Yemen. Britain is also sending an Atlas A400M transport aircraft and military advisers, and extending air-to-air refuelling support for Saudi aircraft by 90 days. The deployment follows renewed fighting after a years-long truce in Yemen collapsed in September. A missile strike on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on Oct. 10 killed 13 people and injured 308, Saudi authorities said. Houthi attacks have also hit energy sites and shipping. The Houthis’ blockade and attacks have disrupted oil exports and pushed up energy prices, while Saudi Arabia postponed its flagship Future Investment Initiative conference until 2027. The UK government says its support is defensive, a lasting settlement requires diplomacy and it will continue backing a U.N.-led political process.
world.image_alt: UK sends Typhoon jets to shield Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

world.title: Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads across Africa
world.summary: Nigeria confirmed its first case of the current Ebola outbreak on Oct. 20, after laboratory tests detected the Bundibugyo strain in a woman in the capital, Abuja. She developed symptoms on Oct. 7 and was admitted to a private hospital four days later. Authorities have identified 44 contacts and begun monitoring people
world.content: Nigeria confirmed its first case of the current Ebola outbreak on Oct. 20, after laboratory tests detected the Bundibugyo strain in a woman in the capital, Abuja. She developed symptoms on Oct. 7 and was admitted to a private hospital four days later. Authorities have identified 44 contacts and begun monitoring people who may have been exposed. Uganda’s health ministry said she had travelled to eastern Democratic Republic of Congo on business and only transited through Uganda. Where she became infected remains under investigation, the ministry said. The outbreak, declared in Congo in May, has spread across central, eastern and now western Africa. Congo had reported 9,552 confirmed infections and 4,602 deaths, while Kenya confirmed its ninth case on Oct. 20. Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya put the outbreak’s fatality rate at about 48%. Nigeria says its patient is isolated and receiving care. Health authorities are strengthening infection controls at the hospital and urging facilities nationwide to prepare for suspected cases. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) is coordinating the response, while the World Health Organization (WHO) and partners are supporting case investigations, contact tracing and the provision of protective equipment.
world.image_alt: Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads across Africa

world.title: Italy deploys 500 troops and enacts tougher protest laws after Milan riots
world.summary: Italy’s cabinet approved a decree on Tuesday deploying 500 soldiers to Milan through the end of 2026 and introducing tougher penalties after cost-of-living protests turned violent in the city and other northern towns. The decree took effect immediately, but parliament must convert it into law within 60 days. The decree
world.content: Italy’s cabinet approved a decree on Tuesday deploying 500 soldiers to Milan through the end of 2026 and introducing tougher penalties after cost-of-living protests turned violent in the city and other northern towns. The decree took effect immediately, but parliament must convert it into law within 60 days. The decree creates an offence for people in groups of five or more who endanger public safety during a demonstration, punishable by up to five years in prison and a €20,000 fine. It also makes parents liable for damage caused by their children and presumes that people aged 14 and over understand their actions unless proven otherwise. Police said more than 100 officers were injured over the weekend, when young people looted shops and set fires. Demonstrators cited fuel and energy costs, rents, low wages and poor public services. Separately, truckers in southern Italy have blocked roads over diesel prices, disrupting supply chains and forcing some pasta makers to halt production. A new round of demonstrations is planned for Saturday, Oct. 24. Parliament will decide whether the measures become permanent law.
world.image_alt: Italy deploys 500 troops and enacts tougher protest laws after Milan riots

business.title: Walmart bundles Walmart+ and Sam
business.summary: Walmart launched a $120 annual membership combining Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus on Oct. 20, charging nearly $100 less than the two plans purchased separately. The bundle includes delivery from both retailers, Sam’s Club warehouse access and member prices, 10 cents off gas at more than 17,000 stations, 2% rewards on el
business.content: Walmart launched a $120 annual membership combining Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus on Oct. 20, charging nearly $100 less than the two plans purchased separately. The bundle includes delivery from both retailers, Sam’s Club warehouse access and member prices, 10 cents off gas at more than 17,000 stations, 2% rewards on eligible Sam’s Club purchases, and a choice of Peacock or Paramount+ streaming. The offer is aimed at attracting shoppers seeking convenience and savings while increasing recurring membership revenue. Existing Walmart+ annual members can upgrade for $22 more; Sam’s Club Plus members can add Walmart+ at no extra cost, and customers who already hold both memberships can link their accounts. The combined plan has no monthly payment option, and both standalone memberships remain available.

business.title: Salesforce to buy AI marketing platform Braze for $5.66 billion
business.summary: Salesforce agreed on Oct. 20 to acquire Braze, a customer-engagement software company, for about $5.66 billion in cash, offering Braze shareholders $47.50 per share. The offer is about 58% above Braze’s previous closing price. Salesforce said Braze’s tools will strengthen its marketing products with software that perso
business.content: Salesforce agreed on Oct. 20 to acquire Braze, a customer-engagement software company, for about $5.66 billion in cash, offering Braze shareholders $47.50 per share. The offer is about 58% above Braze’s previous closing price. Salesforce said Braze’s tools will strengthen its marketing products with software that personalizes messages and responds to customer behavior in real time. The deal is expected to close in Salesforce’s fiscal 2028, subject to Braze shareholder and regulatory approvals; Salesforce said it does not expect the deal to affect its fiscal 2027 forecast. The acquisition follows Salesforce’s $3.6 billion agreement for AI customer-service platform Fin earlier this year and its $8 billion acquisition of Informatica last year.
business.image_alt: Salesforce to buy AI marketing platform Braze for $5.66 billion

business.title: Jio IPO fully subscribed in 100 minutes as institutions lead demand
business.summary: Jio Platforms, Reliance Industries’ telecom and digital-services unit, drew full subscription for its 30,213-crore-rupee ($3.2 billion) initial public offering within about 100 minutes of opening on Oct. 21. The offering is India’s largest share sale to date. Qualified institutional buyers drove early demand, while bid
business.content: Jio Platforms, Reliance Industries’ telecom and digital-services unit, drew full subscription for its 30,213-crore-rupee ($3.2 billion) initial public offering within about 100 minutes of opening on Oct. 21. The offering is India’s largest share sale to date. Qualified institutional buyers drove early demand, while bids in the retail and non-institutional categories remained below their reserved allocations in opening-day updates. The fresh issue, priced at 1,065 to 1,119 rupees per share, values Jio at about $108 billion at the top of the range; existing shareholders are not selling shares in the offering. Jio plans to use up to 27,500 crore rupees of the proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings at its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm, with the balance for general corporate purposes. The company reported FY2026 revenue of 146,885 crore rupees and net profit of 30,049 crore rupees, with telecom accounting for about 90% of both. The offer closes Oct. 23, allotment is expected Oct. 26 and trading is scheduled to begin Oct. 28.
business.image_alt: Jio IPO fully subscribed in 100 minutes as institutions lead demand

business.title: UK inflation rises to 3.5% as motor-fuel prices jump 29.8%
business.summary: UK annual consumer-price inflation rose to 3.5% in September from 3.1% in August, above economists’ 3.4% forecast, as motor-fuel prices rose 29.8% over the year. Fuel was the biggest upward driver, while services inflation increased to 3.7% from 3.4% and core inflation, excluding food, energy, alcohol and tobacco, reac
business.content: UK annual consumer-price inflation rose to 3.5% in September from 3.1% in August, above economists’ 3.4% forecast, as motor-fuel prices rose 29.8% over the year. Fuel was the biggest upward driver, while services inflation increased to 3.7% from 3.4% and core inflation, excluding food, energy, alcohol and tobacco, reached 2.8%. The annual rate was the highest since October 2025. Financial markets priced in a 98% chance that the Bank of England would raise its key rate by a quarter point to 4% in November, with many traders also expecting another increase in December. Finance Minister John Healey will present his first budget on Oct. 28, with higher borrowing costs limiting funds for household support. Healey has said the budget will maintain fiscal discipline while seeking growth and relief for families and businesses.
business.image_alt: UK inflation rises to 3.5% as motor-fuel prices jump 29.8%

business.title: Canadian dollar hits four-week high after Alberta vote
business.summary: The Canadian dollar climbed to a four-week high on Oct. 20, gaining about 0.5% to 1.4045 per U.S. dollar after Alberta voters rejected beginning a separation process. It touched 1.4033, its strongest intraday level since Sept. 22. Bloomberg reported a gain of as much as 0.55%, the currency’s best session since Sept. 22
business.content: The Canadian dollar climbed to a four-week high on Oct. 20, gaining about 0.5% to 1.4045 per U.S. dollar after Alberta voters rejected beginning a separation process. It touched 1.4033, its strongest intraday level since Sept. 22. Bloomberg reported a gain of as much as 0.55%, the currency’s best session since Sept. 22. The result removed one source of political uncertainty in Alberta, a province central to Canada’s oil economy. The rally also reflected stronger expectations of a Bank of Canada rate increase, which helped narrow the yield gap with the United States. Markets were pricing in an 80% chance of a quarter-point increase to 2.50% at the central bank’s Oct. 28 meeting, Reuters reported.
business.image_alt: Canadian dollar hits four-week high after Alberta vote

business.title: U.S. housing starts fall 5.2% as high rates deter buyers
business.summary: U.S. housing starts fell 5.2% in September to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.221 million, while contracts to buy existing homes dropped 7.3%, pushing the pending-sales index to a record low of 66.0. Starts were 7.4% below a year earlier, and pending sales fell in all four U.S. regions. The average 30-year fixed
business.content: U.S. housing starts fell 5.2% in September to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.221 million, while contracts to buy existing homes dropped 7.3%, pushing the pending-sales index to a record low of 66.0. Starts were 7.4% below a year earlier, and pending sales fell in all four U.S. regions. The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.40% last week, its highest level in nearly three years, while homebuilder sentiment fell in October to its lowest since 2012. Builders also face higher material and labor costs, and unsold new homes have reduced the incentive to begin projects, even as a national housing shortage keeps home prices elevated. Goldman Sachs forecast further declines in residential investment over the next three quarters, while Nationwide Financial’s Ben Ayers said construction could remain subdued into 2027. The government was due to release its advance estimate of third-quarter GDP the following week, and investors expected the Federal Reserve to hold rates at its next meeting.
business.image_alt: U.S. housing starts fall 5.2% as high rates deter buyers

business.title: SpaceX swings to $4.4 billion profit as AI sales surge
business.summary: SpaceX, the rocket and artificial-intelligence company led by Chief Executive Elon Musk, reported $4.4 billion in net income for the July-September quarter, reversing a $541 million loss in the previous quarter as revenue climbed 161% year over year to $14.6 billion. Its Super Intelligence division, which includes comp
business.content: SpaceX, the rocket and artificial-intelligence company led by Chief Executive Elon Musk, reported $4.4 billion in net income for the July-September quarter, reversing a $541 million loss in the previous quarter as revenue climbed 161% year over year to $14.6 billion. Its Super Intelligence division, which includes computing services, the Grok chatbot and acquired coding startup Cursor, generated $7.56 billion in sales, up 830% from a year earlier; Starlink satellite internet revenue rose 69% to $5.25 billion. The AI unit recorded $431 million in operating income, while SpaceX spent $19.6 billion on capital projects during the quarter, including $16.4 billion on AI infrastructure. Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen forecast first-quarter 2027 revenue of $33 billion to $37 billion, citing stronger visibility into computing contracts. Musk also said SpaceX and electric-vehicle maker Tesla had formed independent board committees to examine a possible merger, which he said would require approval from at least 50% of Tesla shareholders.
business.image_alt: SpaceX swings to $4.4 billion profit as AI sales surge

business.title: France deploys troops as bond yields hit 24-year high
business.summary: France will deploy troops alongside police for protests on Saturday, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said, after Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez acknowledged failures in the response to the Oct. 17 unrest. Investors have been selling French assets: the 10-year government bond yield reached 4.98% on Tuesday, a 24-year
business.content: France will deploy troops alongside police for protests on Saturday, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said, after Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez acknowledged failures in the response to the Oct. 17 unrest. Investors have been selling French assets: the 10-year government bond yield reached 4.98% on Tuesday, a 24-year high, while the CAC 40 stock index is down 10% from its August peak. The demonstrations began with student complaints about schools and widened to anger over living costs and public services. France’s public debt stood at 119% of gross domestic product at the end of June, and the government expects the deficit to reach 5.4% of GDP this year. The government plans to mobilize a “massive” security presence and impose curfews where needed; it also aims to cut the 2027 deficit to 5% of GDP. Parliament faces budget negotiations, while France’s presidential election is scheduled for April 2027.
business.image_alt: France deploys troops as bond yields hit 24-year high

science.title: International study links varied social activity to stronger cognition in older adults
science.summary: An analysis of five long-term studies found that older adults who took part in social activities had higher cognitive scores than those who did not, with the strongest association among people involved in at least three activities. The study pooled data on 57,793 people across 24 countries. Average ages in the study gr
science.content: An analysis of five long-term studies found that older adults who took part in social activities had higher cognitive scores than those who did not, with the strongest association among people involved in at least three activities. The study pooled data on 57,793 people across 24 countries. Average ages in the study groups ranged from 57 to 73, and participants were followed for an average of six years. The findings were published in the *Journal of Epidemiology & Community Health*. Volunteering and sports-club membership were associated with a lower risk of cognitive decline across all five study groups, but the researchers stressed that the observational design cannot show that social activity causes better cognition. Participants reported their own activities, and the researchers said differences among surveys and incomplete adjustment for other factors limit the findings.
science.image_alt: International study links varied social activity to stronger cognition in older adults

science.title: Tesla
science.summary: Tesla demonstrated a prototype Roadster at a SpaceX test facility in Texas on Oct. 15. The car climbed a steep ramp, hung upside down, flipped off and made short jumps using compressed-air jets, with no driver aboard. Tesla says production is planned for 2028, but the display did not show sustained flight. The company
science.content: Tesla demonstrated a prototype Roadster at a SpaceX test facility in Texas on Oct. 15. The car climbed a steep ramp, hung upside down, flipped off and made short jumps using compressed-air jets, with no driver aboard. Tesla says production is planned for 2028, but the display did not show sustained flight. The company says the car combines high-pressure air thrusters with an underbody suction system, but the demonstration did not establish whether it can safely fly or operate on public roads. Roger Connor, curator for vertical flight at the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, said a car-aircraft hybrid faces a basic weight trade-off. Computer scientist Yann LeCun questioned whether the demonstration vehicle had enough equipment for practical use. Tesla has not allowed journalists to inspect the vehicle, leaving questions about its configuration unresolved.

science.title: Study finds rule-breakers can push groups toward wider violations
science.summary: A behavioral experiment with 750 U.S. participants found that people were more likely to imitate rule-breaking than rule-following, especially when the person they observed shared their political affiliation. Participants chose the brightest square in a row of 100, but earned more money by choosing squares farther to t
science.content: A behavioral experiment with 750 U.S. participants found that people were more likely to imitate rule-breaking than rule-following, especially when the person they observed shared their political affiliation. Participants chose the brightest square in a row of 100, but earned more money by choosing squares farther to the right, against the instruction to select the brightest one. Just over 4% of participants escalated beyond the violation they observed, and computer simulations showed that a small number of such people could drive much broader rule-breaking. The researchers caution that the experiment was abstract and imposed no penalty for breaking the rule; psychologist Stephen Reicher of the University of St Andrews said its relevance to real-world events remains unproven.
science.image_alt: Study finds rule-breakers can push groups toward wider violations

science.title: Global heat storms rise to 102 a year, Reuters analysis finds
science.summary: An analysis of hourly temperatures across more than 1 million grid squares worldwide found that large heat waves—termed “heat storms” in the analysis—increased from about five active events a year in the 1960s to 102 a year this decade. Reuters developed the term after consulting two dozen climate researchers; it defin
science.content: An analysis of hourly temperatures across more than 1 million grid squares worldwide found that large heat waves—termed “heat storms” in the analysis—increased from about five active events a year in the 1960s to 102 a year this decade. Reuters developed the term after consulting two dozen climate researchers; it defines a heat storm as a heat wave lasting at least five days and covering at least 1% of Earth at its peak. Heat Storm Vera, the largest identified, lasted 367 days in 2023-24 and reached nearly 85% of the globe. The current named event, Heat Storm Raimundo, began on February 28, 2026, and had reached almost three-quarters of Earth’s surface by October. The analysis also found that a chain of overlapping heat storms has continued somewhere on the planet since July 6, 2008.
science.image_alt: Global heat storms rise to 102 a year, Reuters analysis finds

science.title: Researchers warn AI agents could erode human skills and agency
science.summary: Researchers and security officials warn that expanding AI use could weaken human capabilities and increase the risks of misuse. A scenario called “gradual disempowerment” describes people losing skills as AI takes over more tasks and decisions. MI5 chief Sir Ken McCallum has also warned that AI could “change the stakes
science.content: Researchers and security officials warn that expanding AI use could weaken human capabilities and increase the risks of misuse. A scenario called “gradual disempowerment” describes people losing skills as AI takes over more tasks and decisions. MI5 chief Sir Ken McCallum has also warned that AI could “change the stakes” for existing and new biological weapons. A paper published in early 2025 introduced the term “gradual disempowerment,” and researchers say the concern extends beyond job displacement to the loss of human judgment. Nobel-winning AI researcher Geoffrey Hinton has argued that AI may have subjective experience, but that claim remains unproven and disputed. Microsoft executive Mustafa Suleyman argues that consciousness is biological. Margaret Mitchell, an AI research scientist at Hugging Face, warned that people who stop practicing skills may lose the ability to use them.
science.image_alt: Researchers warn AI agents could erode human skills and agency

science.title: SpaceX plans first catch of both Starship stages in November
science.summary: SpaceX plans to try catching both stages of its Starship rocket during a test flight targeted for November, chief executive Elon Musk said Oct. 20. The Super Heavy booster and Ship spacecraft are designed to return to the launch tower, where mechanical arms would catch them. Success would mark the first full recovery o
science.content: SpaceX plans to try catching both stages of its Starship rocket during a test flight targeted for November, chief executive Elon Musk said Oct. 20. The Super Heavy booster and Ship spacecraft are designed to return to the launch tower, where mechanical arms would catch them. Success would mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch vehicle, Musk said. The attempt follows 14 Starship test flights, including three in which SpaceX caught the booster, but the company has never caught the spacecraft. Ship returns from a longer flight at a higher speed, making its recovery more demanding. Flight 14 reached orbit and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites on Sept. 28, but an engine shutdown shortened the mission, and both stages splashed down without recovery. Musk said flight attempts would continue through year-end if the November effort fails.
science.image_alt: SpaceX plans first catch of both Starship stages in November

science.title: Macaques exposed to deadly outbreak avoid contaminated-looking food more often
science.summary: Japanese macaques that lived through a deadly 2020 outbreak at a southern Texas primate sanctuary were later more likely to avoid food that looked contaminated, researchers reported in a study published in Royal Society Open Science. In tests involving 55 monkeys, outbreak-exposed groups ate food displayed over macaque
science.content: Japanese macaques that lived through a deadly 2020 outbreak at a southern Texas primate sanctuary were later more likely to avoid food that looked contaminated, researchers reported in a study published in Royal Society Open Science. In tests involving 55 monkeys, outbreak-exposed groups ate food displayed over macaque feces in 47% of trials, compared with 79% for monkeys from an unexposed group. The virus spreads through bites and scratches, not contaminated food. The exposed monkeys behaved similarly whether they had been infected or not, suggesting that experiencing the outbreak was associated with increased caution. Researchers did not measure disgust directly.
science.image_alt: Macaques exposed to deadly outbreak avoid contaminated-looking food more often

science.title: Australian researchers propose body-clock depression subtype affecting one-quarter
science.summary: Researchers at the University of Sydney propose a “circadian” subtype of depression linked to disrupted body-clock patterns, based on 2,604 of 11,380 Australians with severe, recurrent or persistent depression who met the proposed criteria. These participants reported late sleep schedules, seasonal mood changes and wak
science.content: Researchers at the University of Sydney propose a “circadian” subtype of depression linked to disrupted body-clock patterns, based on 2,604 of 11,380 Australians with severe, recurrent or persistent depression who met the proposed criteria. These participants reported late sleep schedules, seasonal mood changes and waking tired, as well as less benefit and more side effects from common antidepressants. The subtype is not yet formally established, and the study relied on participants’ reports of sleep and medication experiences. Experts say more research is needed before the findings guide clinical practice. The researchers suggest studying light therapy, melatonin and behavioral approaches targeting circadian rhythms, but clinical trials and validation in other populations are still needed.
science.image_alt: Australian researchers propose body-clock depression subtype affecting one-quarter

sports.title: Rays, Brewers meet in World Series that guarantees a first-time champion
sports.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers begin the World Series on Friday, Oct. 23, in a best-of-seven matchup that guarantees one franchise its first championship. Tampa Bay is making its third Series appearance, while Milwaukee returns for the first time since 1982; the teams finished with 98 and 103 regular-season w
sports.content: The Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers begin the World Series on Friday, Oct. 23, in a best-of-seven matchup that guarantees one franchise its first championship. Tampa Bay is making its third Series appearance, while Milwaukee returns for the first time since 1982; the teams finished with 98 and 103 regular-season wins, respectively. Tampa Bay won three straight games to close out the American League Championship Series, while Milwaukee swept the Los Angeles Dodgers in four games to win the National League pennant. Both teams rely on defense, pitching and versatile offenses. Milwaukee holds home-field advantage after posting baseball’s best regular-season record. Both clubs rank among the league’s lower-spending teams. Major League Baseball owners have proposed a salary cap and floor, the players’ association rejects a cap, and a lockout is likely to begin Dec. 2.

sports.title: Giants release veteran running back Najee Harris after five games

sports.content: The New York Giants released running back Najee Harris on Tuesday, two days after he started in a 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints and gained two yards on four carries. Harris, 28, finished his five-game stint with the Giants with 99 rushing yards on 31 carries, averaging 3.2 yards per attempt. The Giants are weighing how to divide carries among running backs Cam Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary before their next game against the Houston Texans. Giants coach John Harbaugh said none had earned a featured role; ESPN reported that Harris’ postgame criticism of the rotation was not the reason for his release.

sports.title: Football watchdog can force Manchester City owners to sell if verdict stands
sports.summary: David Kogan, chair of England’s Independent Football Regulator, says the watchdog can force Manchester City’s owners to sell if the club is ultimately found to have been run improperly. He said it is too early to decide whether the regulator will open its own investigation while City’s appeal is pending. An independent
sports.content: David Kogan, chair of England’s Independent Football Regulator, says the watchdog can force Manchester City’s owners to sell if the club is ultimately found to have been run improperly. He said it is too early to decide whether the regulator will open its own investigation while City’s appeal is pending. An independent commission found that City breached 114 of 115 Premier League financial rules covering 2009 to 2018, including through commercial arrangements said to have inflated revenue or reduced costs by more than £900 million. The club denies wrongdoing and has appealed, saying the ruling contains material errors and the evidence supports its case. The Financial Reporting Council, a separate UK accounting watchdog, is examining the commission’s findings for possible implications for City’s financial statements and external audits. Reports have suggested a points deduction large enough to relegate City, potentially alongside a fine, but no punishment has been announced. Under the current timetable, the appeal could conclude by mid-December, with a sanctions decision following in early 2027. Legal challenges could delay the process.

sports.title: Foden hat-trick lifts Manchester City past AEK Athens 5-1
sports.summary: Manchester City midfielder Phil Foden scored three goals and set up another as his side beat AEK Athens 5-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday for their second win in the Champions League league phase. Elliot Anderson scored his first City goal and Rayan Cherki added the hosts’ third; Stavros Pilios briefly made it 2-1 b
sports.content: Manchester City midfielder Phil Foden scored three goals and set up another as his side beat AEK Athens 5-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday for their second win in the Champions League league phase. Elliot Anderson scored his first City goal and Rayan Cherki added the hosts’ third; Stavros Pilios briefly made it 2-1 before City pulled away. The result followed City’s 4-2 loss to Paris Saint-Germain. Foden had gone about 10 months without scoring before finding the net against Ipswich Town on Saturday. Against AEK, he scored twice more to complete his first hat-trick in more than two years. Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca made eight changes and rested striker Erling Haaland because of a foot concern, while 17-year-old academy forward Floyd Samba started. City’s next Champions League fixture is away to RB Leipzig on November 4; AEK host Real Madrid.

sports.title: South Africa captain Bavuma scores 179 in second Test against Australia
sports.summary: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma scored a career-best 179 to take his team from 110-6 to 425-9 declared and a first-innings lead of 133 runs in the second Test against Australia in Gqeberha. Australia ended day three at 3-1, still 422 runs behind, after fast bowler Kagiso Rabada dismissed Nic Maddinson for a duck. Bav
sports.content: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma scored a career-best 179 to take his team from 110-6 to 425-9 declared and a first-innings lead of 133 runs in the second Test against Australia in Gqeberha. Australia ended day three at 3-1, still 422 runs behind, after fast bowler Kagiso Rabada dismissed Nic Maddinson for a duck. Bavuma spent more than nine hours at the crease, facing 334 balls and hitting 18 fours and a six. Marco Jansen made 85 and Simon Harmer 82, helping South Africa recover after rain curtailed the first two days. Scott Boland took five wickets for Australia. Australia won the opening Test in Durban by 214 runs and lead the three-match series 1-0. South Africa need to win in Gqeberha to draw level before the final Test in Cape Town. Australia enter day four with nine first-innings wickets remaining.

sports.title: Ten Hag accuses Ronaldo of failing to meet Manchester United’s training standards
sports.summary: Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has accused Cristiano Ronaldo of failing to meet the club’s training and fitness standards during their time together. He said the forward missed sessions and completed only two of three running laps after United’s 4-0 defeat by Brentford in August 2022. Ten Hag also allege
sports.content: Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has accused Cristiano Ronaldo of failing to meet the club’s training and fitness standards during their time together. He said the forward missed sessions and completed only two of three running laps after United’s 4-0 defeat by Brentford in August 2022. Ten Hag also alleged that Ronaldo urged teammates to “save your legs” in training. Ten Hag said players first needed to build their fitness. The Dutchman said he had included Ronaldo in his plans and travelled to Portugal before taking the United job to discuss them. Their relationship deteriorated after Ronaldo refused to come on as a substitute against Tottenham in October 2022. Ronaldo later said he felt betrayed by the club and did not respect Ten Hag. United and Ronaldo ended his contract by mutual agreement the following month. Ronaldo has not commented on Ten Hag’s latest interview. Ten Hag also accused United’s leadership of breaking promises, including an agreement not to sell midfielder Scott McTominay. He said he wanted the club to pursue Harry Kane and Declan Rice, and described disagreements and poor communication with the leadership.

sports.content: Iga Swiatek, Poland’s six-time Grand Slam champion, has ended her 2026 season after withdrawing from the Ningbo Open with a persistent left-thigh injury. The withdrawal ended her bid to qualify for the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, scheduled for Nov. 8-15. Ranked ninth in the qualifying race, she needed to reach at least the quarterfinals in Ningbo to stay in contention. The same thigh problem hampered Swiatek in her Wuhan Open semifinal defeat to compatriot Maja Chwalinska, who went on to win the tournament. Swiatek said the injury had persisted for weeks and she needed more time to recover fully. She described the season as one of the most demanding of her career and said she was proud of her team’s progress in the second half of the year. Her withdrawal leaves Karolina Muchova and Marta Kostyuk competing for the final WTA Finals place.

sports.title: Tottenham midfielder Maddison apologises to Coventry fans over badge kiss
sports.summary: Tottenham midfielder James Maddison apologised Tuesday to Coventry City supporters for kissing the Spurs badge after scoring against his boyhood club in Monday’s 3-1 Premier League win. He said he had planned the celebration to thank Tottenham for supporting him and his family through 18 months of injury, and apologise
sports.content: Tottenham midfielder James Maddison apologised Tuesday to Coventry City supporters for kissing the Spurs badge after scoring against his boyhood club in Monday’s 3-1 Premier League win. He said he had planned the celebration to thank Tottenham for supporting him and his family through 18 months of injury, and apologised to anyone who thought the timing was wrong. Maddison, who made his first start in 536 days, said he still loves Coventry and will always be a fan. He played 69 minutes as Tottenham managed his workload; he said he felt able to continue but understood the cautious approach. Tottenham’s next match is away to Chelsea on Saturday, Oct. 24.
